title: Codex Integration
intro: One-click switch the model Codex actually calls — a replacement for ccswitch. Two mechanisms are offered:

restart.restartConfirmTitle: Restart Codex to apply the change?
restart.restartConfirmBody: The config has been written to ~/.codex — Codex must restart to pick it up. Restart now? This force-closes Codex Desktop and relaunches it, so any in-progress turn will be interrupted.
restart.restarted: Codex restarted ({{killed}} processes) — it's relaunching now.
restart.launched: Codex wasn't running — launched it now.
restart.restartNoop: Couldn't find Codex Desktop to restart. Launch it manually.
restart.restartUnsupported: One-click restart isn't supported on this platform — restart Codex manually.

prereq.title: How it works + prerequisites / manual config snippets
prereq.subtitle: two modes / auth.json / config.toml / env vars / cc-switch — click to expand

mobileRemote.title: Control this Codex from your phone (official Codex mobile)
mobileRemote.intro: Want to drive this computer's Codex from your phone? Use OpenAI's official Codex mobile/remote. mimo2codex's job is just to keep your ChatGPT login alive (the 'keep login' apply mode below) so that feature keeps working while the model still runs through the proxy.
mobileRemote.step1Title: Sign in to ChatGPT in Codex
mobileRemote.step1Desc: Run `codex login` (Sign in with ChatGPT) on this machine, or make sure you're already logged in.
mobileRemote.step2Desc: Apply a provider/model below — when a real login is detected, mimo2codex keeps it and only redirects the model backend.
mobileRemote.step3Title: Set up Codex mobile in the desktop app
mobileRemote.step3Desc: In Codex desktop, open 'Set up Codex mobile' and scan the QR code from the ChatGPT app on your phone (same OpenAI account).
mobileRemote.step4Desc: Start and approve tasks from the phone; code, files and shell run on this computer — now backed by your mimo2codex provider.
mobileRemote.caveatTitle: Heads up — this combination is best-effort
mobileRemote.caveatBody: The remote relay is OpenAI's infrastructure; mimo2codex can't change it. Whether OpenAI's remote mode actually runs the model through your local proxy (versus forcing its own models) isn't documented — test it and verify in the mimo2codex logs that requests hit the proxy.

modesInfo.applyFile: <1>Write files and enable</1>: physically writes ~/.codex/auth.json and ~/.codex/config.toml, same as ccswitch. <3>Requires a Codex restart</3>. Original files are auto-backed up and one-click restorable.
modesInfo.runtimeOverride: <1>Runtime override only</1>: stores the active (provider, model) inside mimo2codex; selectProvider uses it as a fallback when the client's requested model isn't recognized by any provider — an explicitly-configured model still wins. <3>No Codex restart needed</3>, but Codex must already connect to mimo2codex (first-time setup still needs the option above).

state.title: Current state
state.codexDirHelp: Any absolute path works (it doesn't need to exist yet). Changes take effect immediately — no restart required. Existing backups stay in the old dir.

owner.external: external (real OpenAI key or another tool)

thinking.title: Thinking mode (global default)
thinking.forceHighSideEffect: ⚠️ Force-high is ON: mimo2codex injects reasoning_effort="high" into every request (even when Codex didn't ask for reasoning). Side effects: (1) trivial requests (hi, single-file reads) also go through reasoning — more tokens, higher latency; (2) on some models 'high' equals 'max', so your bill can rise sharply. Enable only when you really need to see the thought process.
thinking.hint: Thinking ON/OFF: when OFF, every provider skips thinking (mimo / deepseek send thinking:{type:"disabled"}, sensenova / other generic send reasoning_effort:"none"). When ON, each provider follows its own default (most clients don't include reasoning effort for non-GPT-5 models, so the upstream may skip thinking on simple tasks). Force high reasoning effort: only available while Thinking is ON — if Codex didn't pass an effort, mimo2codex injects reasoning_effort="high"; if Codex did pass one, that value is respected. Takes effect immediately (no restart).
thinking.cliOverride: Thinking ON/OFF is currently controlled by CLI flag (--disable-thinking) or env (MIMO2CODEX_DISABLE_THINKING). The switch is locked. Restart without those args to control via UI.

visionFallback.title: Multimodal Fallback
visionFallback.scopeNote: Currently only MiMo models are supported. Other providers/models are not supported yet.
visionFallback.statusOn: Enabled: image requests auto-switch to vision model
visionFallback.hint: When enabled, if a request contains images but the current model doesn't support vision (e.g. mimo-v2.5-pro), automatically switch to the specified multimodal model (default: mimo-v2.5) to avoid images being silently dropped.

superMode.title: Super Mode
superMode.hint: When enabled, every request is debated by two model instances with no round limit. An arbitrator judges whether consensus is reached. A third instance then executes the consensus. Debate auto-stops on client disconnect.
superMode.warning: Super Mode is ON: unlimited debate rounds until the arbitrator declares consensus. Token usage and latency depend on debate complexity. Enable only when high-quality reasoning is needed.

targets.title: Available combinations
targets.externalWarn: Your current ~/.codex/auth.json is a real login (likely Sign in with ChatGPT). 'Write files and enable' now keeps it intact by default and only redirects the model — your ChatGPT login (and OpenAI's official Codex mobile/remote) keeps working. You can still opt to overwrite it in the confirm dialog.
targets.testAllHint: Probes every provider's default model that has an API key configured
targets.restrictedTip: Apply to enable; API / pay-as-you-go (sk-) key only — subscription / token-plan can't use it.
targets.applyTitle: Writes ~/.codex/auth.json and config.toml — requires Codex restart
targets.overrideTitle: Persist active model in settings DB — no Codex restart needed
targets.overrideDisabledTitle: Provider has no API key — cannot be used as runtime override
targets.probeTitle: Send a minimal request to verify the link (key / baseUrl / model id)

override.title: Runtime override
override.empty: No runtime override set. Click 'Runtime override only' on any row above to enable.

backup.title: Backup & restore
backup.intro: Each 'Write files and enable' auto-backs up the current auth.json + config.toml. The most recent 10 are kept; 🔒-marked backups (the first one captured when overwriting your real Codex config) are kept permanently and won't be pruned.
backup.empty: No backups yet. The first 'Write files and enable' will produce one automatically.

type.preservedTitle: Captured the first time we overwrote an external auth.json; kept permanently

backup.deletePreservedTitle: Locked — deleting would permanently lose the original config

msg.applied: Wrote {{provider}} / {{model}}. {{note}}Fully quit and restart Codex for the new config to take effect.
msg.appliedPreserved: Backed up your original Codex config (ts={{ts}}, 🔒 kept permanently — won't be pruned by later switches).
msg.appliedPreservedLogin: Kept your ChatGPT login intact — only the model backend was redirected to mimo2codex (auth.json untouched; ts={{ts}} backup available).
msg.overrideSet: Runtime override set to {{provider}} / {{model}}. No Codex restart needed — the next request will pick it up.
msg.overrideCleared: Runtime override cleared — routing falls back to default behavior.
msg.restored: Restored from backup ts={{ts}}. Restart Codex for the old config to take effect.

confirm.applyP1: Your current ~/.codex/auth.json was not written by mimo2codex and may contain your real OpenAI login.
confirm.applyP2: Proceeding will back it up (auth.json.bak.<ts>) and write a mimo2codex placeholder key. You can restore from 'Backup & restore' below.
confirm.preserveP1: Your ~/.codex/auth.json is a real login (likely Sign in with ChatGPT). mimo2codex will keep it exactly as-is and only rewrite config.toml to route the model through the proxy.
confirm.preserveP2: Your ChatGPT login stays valid, so OpenAI's official Codex mobile/remote keeps working. The current config.toml is backed up first (one-click restore below).
confirm.preserveOverwriteOpt: Overwrite the login instead (write a placeholder key — logs you out of ChatGPT)
confirm.restoreBody: The current auth.json + config.toml will NOT be backed up again.
confirm.restoreMissingAuth: auth.json (did not exist at the time → restore will delete the current auth.json)
confirm.restoreMissingToml: config.toml (did not exist at the time → restore will delete the current config.toml)
confirm.deletePreserved:
This is a '🔒 Original Codex config' backup — deleting it permanently removes the ability to restore your initial real Codex config.

Proceed?
confirm.deleteNormal: Delete backup ts={{ts}}? This is irreversible.
